 Faker Commemorative Stamps Near Sell-Out on Release Day
 Faker Commemorative Stamps Near Sell-Out on Release Day
 Hundreds of collectors queue in Seoul for Faker commemorative stamps.
 BY Probaho Santra 24 OCT 2026, 04:26 PM Share Highlights
 Faker stamps draw strong demand across South Korea.
 Collectors queue overnight at the Seoul Central Post Office for the release.
 Korea Post celebrates Faker’s career with a dedicated stamp collection and exhibition.
 South Korea’s commemorative stamps honoring League of Legends star Lee Sang-hyeok, known as Faker, nearly sold out within half a day of their Oct. 23, 2026, release. Korea Post reported that its entire online allocation was gone by morning, while hundreds of collectors continued queuing at Seoul Central Post Office.
 Korea Post chief, Park In-hwan, shared the update on X, thanking buyers who waited in the cold and postal staff who maintained safety and order. Around 400 people had queued overnight from Oct. 22, with another 400 reportedly waiting when he posted.
 What Does the Faker Commemorative Stamp Collection Include? 
 Korea Post announced an issuance of 140,000 stamp sheets and stamp albums on Oct. 10. The collection traces Faker’s journey from his 2013 professional debut through his rise in competitive League of Legends . The Korea Postal Service Promotion Agency revealed designs for first-day covers and maximum cards on Oct. 14.
 The release also includes photocard-style commemorative stamp cards and personalized stamps. A limited edition comprises 507 individually numbered metal cards, referencing Faker’s May 7 birthday. Meanwhile, Card number 57 is reserved for the player.
 Faker also promoted the collection on social media before its launch.
 Korea Post Recognizes Faker’s Esports Legacy 
 Faker has won six League of Legends World Championship titles and 10 League of Legends Champions Korea (LCK) titles. In January 2026, he became the first esports player to receive South Korea’s Cheongnyong (Blue Dragon) Medal , the highest grade of the country’s Order of Sport Merit.
 On Oct. 10, Korea Post opened the Faker Special Exhibition Hall at the Stamp Museum inside Seoul Central Post Office. The exhibition even features commemorative stamps, video screenings, player uniforms, and a gaming experience area.
 Park stated that Korea Post would continue issuing meaningful stamps that appeal to “all generations, not just the younger generation.” He also expressed support for Faker’s pursuit of a seventh world title and a fourth consecutive championship, known as a “Four-peat.”
